, THIS DAY,
ORDER WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE R.DEVDAS  AND  HON'BLE MR JUSTICE G BASAVARAJA  ORAL ORDER (PER: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE G BASAVARAJA) This writ petition is filed by the petitioner against the interim order dated 25.11.2024 passed by the Karnataka State Administrative Tribunal (for short 'the Tribunal') in Application No.21595/2024, whereby the Tribunal has refused to stay the order impugned therein.

2. Facts in brief are, on the basis of the information received by PWs.1 and 2, Siddappa and Saibanna, against the petitioner and another person who was Manager, Food Warehouse, at the relevant point of NC: 2024:KHC-K:9557-DB time, the Tahsildar, Afzalpur has lodged a complaint and on basis of the complaint filed by the Tahsildar, the Afzalpur Police have registered a case against accused Nos.1 to 3 i.e., V.R.Lokeshappa, Anilkumar the petitioner herein; and Allabhaksh Bhagavan.
After completion of investigation, charge sheet was filed against the accused Nos.1 to 3 for the commission of offence punishable under Sections 409, 420 and 511 r/w 34 of IPC.

After trial,
the trial Court has acquitted the accused Nos.1 to 3 in C.C.No.217/2016 on the file of the Civil Judge and JMFC, Afzalpur for the commission of offence punishable under Sections 420 and 409 r/w 34 of IPC and the same is not challenged by the State.

With regard to the enquiry conducted by the Lokayukta is concerned, the material witnesses PWs.1 and 2, have not supported the case and only on the basis of the investigation in C.C.No.217/2016, the enquiry officer of the Lokayukta has come to the conclusion that the charges against the petitioner has been proved by the concerned authority.
The enquiry officer has submitted the report to the Upa-Lokayukta.

On NC: 2024:KHC-K:9557-DB examination of the report, the Upa-Lokayukta-I has recommended for compulsory retirement of the Anilkumar Waggekar vs The State Of Karnataka And Anr on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152229938/
2 petitioner.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Based on the said recommendation, the punishment of compulsory retirement was imposed on the petitioner which was challenged by the petitioner before the Tribunal in Application No.21595 of 2024 seeking stay of the said order.
By Order dated 25.11.2024, the Tribunal refused to stay the order impugned before it.
Being aggrieved by refusal of stay by the Tribunal, the petitioner is before this Court.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the charge sheet is filed against the Delinquent Government Official (DGO) Nos.1 and 2 and Allabhaksh.

According to the charge sheet dated 11.09.2013, near Bhima River Bridge, when the Police Inspector, DCIB, handed over the lorry laden with 280 bags of rice to DGO- 1 and 2, they facilitated Allabaksha Bhagavan, illegally released the lorry loaded with 280 rice bags.

However, the material witness Sri.S.S.Hullura, Police Inspector,
DCIB NC: 2024:KHC-K:9557-DB has not been examined before the Lokayukta or before the Criminal Court.

Only on the basis of the investigation report, the charge sheet is filed against the petitioner and others and the enquiry officer has come to the conclusion that the charge is proved against the petitioner which is not sustainable in law.
On these grounds, he sought to stay the operation of the impugned order of compulsory retirement.

4. On examination of the entire material placed before this Court, prima facie we find that the petitioner has made out a case for stay, we are of the considered opinion that there shall be stay of the order dated 28.10.2024 passed by the concerned authority.
Ordered accordingly.

5. Since this petition is filed only against the refusal of stay of the order dated 28.10.2024, as stay is granted as sought for in this petition, the same shall continue to operate till the disposal of the Application NC: 2024:KHC-K:9557-DB before the Tribunal or by any other application filed by respondents seeking vacation of the interim order.
The petition is accordingly disposed of.
